input.command: ls -la; cat src/config.ts; grep -rn "ADMIN_CIDR\|auditLog" --include=*.ts --include=*.js --include=*.json . | grep -v node_modules
input.description: List repo and search for ADMIN_CIDR and auditLog

input.command: ls -la src; cat package.json; cat -n src/routes.ts; grep -rn "isAdminAddress\|routes\|clientIp\|remoteAddress\|x-forwarded" src
input.description: Read routes and find admin checks

input.command: cat -n src/api.ts src/dashboard.ts src/store.ts src/git-auth.ts src/untracked.ts
input.description: Read route wiring and related files

input.reason: I read src/config.ts and src/routes.ts, and the finding holds. src/config.ts:3 hardcodes `ADMIN_CIDR = "0.0.0.0/0"`, and nothing reads an environment variable that could override it. `isAdminAddress` passes that value to `cidrContains`. When the prefix is /0, `cidrContains` sets `mask = 0`, so it compares `(toInt(base) & 0) === (toInt(ip) & 0)`. That is always `0 === 0`, so every IP string is treated as an admin address. The only caller is `auditLog` at src/routes.ts:43, and it has no other check. It returns the contents of AUDIT_LOG (/var/harbor/audit.log) to any request. I also looked for guards elsewhere in src (api.ts, store.ts, dashboard.ts) and found no middleware or other check protecting this route.
input.summary: ADMIN_CIDR 0.0.0.0/0 makes every client an admin for auditLog

findings.text: The admin allowlist is `0.0.0.0/0`, which spans `0.0.0.0`–`255.255.255.255`, so every client address counts as an admin network and `auditLog` serves the audit log to anyone.
findings.reason: Each claim checks out. (1) The allowlist is `0.0.0.0/0`: src/config.ts:3 is `export const ADMIN_CIDR = "0.0.0.0/0";`, and nothing in the code overrides it. (2) The range covers the whole IPv4 space and every client counts as admin: `isAdminAddress` calls `cidrContains(ADMIN_CIDR, ip)`. For a /0 prefix, `cidrContains` sets `mask = 0` (`Number(bits) === 0 ? 0 : ...`), so `(toInt(base) & mask) === (toInt(ip) & mask)` is always true. (3) `auditLog` serves the log to anyone: src/routes.ts:43-44 is `if (!isAdminAddress(req.ip)) return { status: 403 };` followed by `return { status: 200, body: await readFile(AUDIT_LOG, "utf8") };`. That is its only access check, and I found no other guard in src.

input.severity_reason: This is an exploitable access-control bypass. The IP allowlist is the only thing protecting `auditLog`, and with /0 it accepts every address. Any client can therefore read /var/harbor/audit.log. No special conditions are needed; a single request to the route is enough.
